Subject: Legal Review and Recommended Next Steps - LLW Construction Dispute

Good afternoon Ms. Bell and Mr. Devlin,

I hope you are doing well. I wanted to follow up with a summary of our findings after reviewing your construction contract, payment records, and related correspondence for your property at 3414 South Belcher Drive, Tampa, Florida.

As discussed, the primary concern is incomplete and defective contractor work after substantial payment.

Based on our review, you entered a construction agreement and paid $100,000.00, but key work remained incomplete as of March 15, 2025. You also received a Notice to Owner that increased urgency around lien exposure and title risk.

Here are the key points of our analysis:

• Under Florida law, there is an implied warranty of workmanlike construction, which is a legal protection requiring contractors to perform competent work even if the contract is silent. In your situation, the documented incomplete framing and delayed performance support a breach of that protection. What this means for you: you have a viable basis to demand cure, completion, or monetary recovery.

• Florida Statute § 558.004 requires a pre-suit notice-and-opportunity-to-repair process before filing construction defect litigation. Think of this as a required pre-lawsuit step that gives the contractor a defined chance to respond. What this means for you: we should send the Chapter 558 notice promptly so we preserve leverage and comply with the legal process.

• The Notice to Owner is a warning that unpaid project participants may assert lien rights against the property. In practical terms, unresolved lien claims can interfere with selling or refinancing until addressed. What this means for you: protective lien strategy and careful documentation are immediate priorities.

Based on the above, a negotiated resolution is likely the most efficient path forward. We recommend sending a formal demand and required pre-suit notice while preserving all rights under the contract and applicable statutes.

Please let us know if you would like us to proceed with drafting and sending the required notices, or whether you would prefer that we first schedule a call to discuss.

Thank you,
Franklin Riley
Senior Partner
